articles.title: RBI likely selling dollars to limit rupee's fall, traders say

articles.title: MCX shares jump 4% despite overall market weakness. Here's why
articles.content: Multi-Commodity Exchange of India shares surged after the company reported a sharp rise in Q4FY26 earnings. articles.title: Goldman Sachs delays Fed cut outlook to December 2026 as Iran war drives US inflation
articles.content: Goldman Sachs now anticipates U.S. Federal Reserve rate cuts in December 2026 and March 2027, delaying its previous September and December 2024 outlook. Elevated energy prices, driven by the Middle East conflict, are expected to maintain inflation above the Fed's target, prompting caution among policymakers.

articles.title: SBI shares plunge 10% in two days after Q4. Do Morgan Stanley, Citi & Bernstein see a rebound soon?

articles.title: Not just US dollar, Indian rupee has tanked up to 25% across 9 major currencies in 1 year
articles.content: The Indian rupee has seen a significant decline against most global currencies, not just the US dollar. articles.title: Who is your worst enemy in markets? Here’s what Buffett’s mentor Benjamin Graham says
articles.content: Benjamin Graham, Warren Buffett's mentor, identified investors themselves as their worst market enemies, attributing disaster to Wall Street's enthusiasm. He emphasized that temperament, not just knowledge, is key to investment success, advocating for a strong-minded approach based on the margin-of-safety principle. Graham also distinguished between speculation and investment, advising a separate, smaller fund for speculative ventures.

articles.title: Bajaj Auto's Rs 5,633 crore share buyback: Should you participate or avoid?

articles.title: Global Market: Japan bets on BOJ hawkish turn, US backing to defend Yen
articles.content: Japan is stepping up efforts to slow the yen’s decline through a coordinated push involving the Bank of Japan, the Finance Ministry and support from the U.S., with policymakers adopting a more hawkish stance and intervening aggressively in currency markets. Authorities are estimated to have spent nearly 10 trillion yen on yen-buying interventions after concerns grew over inflation risks linked to the weak currency.
